thread.title: Tech Today: Zuck Goes to Washington, PayPal Tops, Tesla’s Stretch

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Zuck Goes to Washington, PayPal Tops, Tesla’s Stretch

organizations.name: u.s. house energy and commerce committee

text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated April 9, 2018 11:03 a.m. ET Here are some things going on today in your world of tech:
Zuck goes to Washington Shares of Facebook ( FB ) are up $1.94, or 1%, at $159.14, as scrutiny of the company’s regulatory vulnerability continues before CEO Mark Zuckerberg testifies before Congress tomorrow.
Reuters ’s David Shepardson writes that Zuckerberg is scheduled to meet with various members of Congress on an individual basis today, before formal testimony before the U.S. Senate Judiciary and Commerce committees on Tuesday, and the U.S. House Energy and Commerce Committee on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, Craig Timberg and Tony Romm wrote yesterday that Facebook could be facing a record fine for having failed to “prevent risks to user data,” and thereby violating a 2011 consent decree signed with the Federal Trade Commission , citing three unnamed sources.
In advance of those meetings, Zuckerberg announced on his page this morning that the company is forming an “an independent election research commission that will solicit research on the effects of social media on elections and democracy ."
Standing up for Facebook Helping Facebook's stock this morning are a couple of fan notes defending the biz. KeyBanc ’s Andy Hargreaves reiterates an Overweight rating and a $245 price target, writing that “despite significant media coverage and investor concern, checks with ad agency executives suggest spending on Facebook remains strong and is likely to grow in line with or ahead of our estimate of 41% y/y constant currency growth in 1Q.”
And Jefferies analyst Brent Thill reiterates a Buy rating, while cutting his price target to $215 from $230, noting that Facebook users aren’t leaving the platform in droves. He did a survey of of 750 US Internet users and found 60% or more use the combined Facebook and Instagram “more often, or the same as a year ago,” which “gives us further confidence that consumers remain on the FB platforms despite recent turmoil."
Europe rules could have a mild impact Among people on the Street considering the impact of regulation on tech companies is Goldman Sachs ’s Heather Bellini , who took a look at the “GDPR,” the gigantic set of European privacy rules that are just about to go into effect.
Those rules require companies such as Facebook and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) to either explicitly gain users’ consent to gather their data — an “opt-in” rather than “opt-out” — or the company must demonstrate a “legitimate interest” to gather the data without consent.
Bellini concludes the impact on Alphabet’s Google’s advertising business would be minimal — perhaps as much as a 2% reduction in ad revenue — but that as much as 7% of Facebook's ad revenue could be at risk.
Alphabet's stock this morning is up $27.77, or 2.8%, at $1,037.72.
PayPal’s still tops For those who worry about competition to payments pioneer PayPal ( PYPL ), Morgan Stanley’s James Faucette , noting all the merchants the company has bagged to accept its payments, urges them to fear not.
PayPal "continues to maintain its online acceptance lead vs. other digital wallets with acceptance at 79% of the top 500 Internet retailers in the US,” writes Faucette, who has an Overweight rating on PayPal. "The next largest accepted digital wallet continues to be Amazon Pay, which added 2 net new merchants this quarter and is now available at 12% of the top 500 websites."
PayPal stock this morning is up $1.85, or 2.5%, at $75.71.
Stay the course on Apple Another day, another check of Apple ’s ( AAPL ) iPhone supply chain. This one comes from RBC Capital ’s Amit Daryanani , who writes that his conversations with Apple’s suppliers indicate the company is planning to make 80 million to 90 million iPhone units in the second half of this year, lower than the 100 million to 120 million that was predicted for last year’s production. Some of that, though, is about "supply chain partners managing inventory levels more diligently," Daryanani explains.
Daryanani reiterates an Outperform rating on Apple stock, and a $203 price target, and reminds investors that they can look forward to Apple’s capital allocation, its growth in services, its potential for “gross-margin upside,” and the stock’s “attractive valuation."
Apple shares are up $3.33, or 2%, at $171.71.
Tesla’s stretch goal Analyst John Donavan of the boutique BlueFin Research Partners writes that Tesla’s ( TSLA ) goal of hitting 5,000 units made per week of its Model 3 sedan is “a stretch” at its current rate of production.
"Given our reads on battery module assembly capabilities/ramps which take 4 per Model 3 battery pack,” writes Donavan, "the only way to hit this lofty goal would be to stockpile batteries until the last half of June and inflate production exiting the quarter in our view."
This follows Tesla disclosure last week of its production numbers for Q1 that missed the company's own forecast. Tesla shares, however, had their best week in a long time despite that shortfall as investors cheered progress.
Tesla shares today are up $9.30, or 3%, at $308.60.
